Purpose and exclusions

Character XP/levels and profession skill are separate durable tracks. The level cap is data-defined; derived combat attributes are rebuilt from class growth, level, equipment, talents and valid effects rather than saved as competing authoritative totals.

Never bypass the declared rule owner, mutate an authored definition at runtime, trust a client completion claim, or infer a compiled implementation from this page.

Creation and configuration

  1. Author DT_LevelThresholds with rows 1..50 and strictly increasing cumulative XP. Start with a small test threshold so Slice B can prove leveling, then restore catalog values.
  2. Create DA_Progression_Default linking class growth and threshold data. Do not hardcode level 50 in widgets.
  3. Add URPGProgressionComponent to PlayerState after native compilation; it owns in-zone read-only projections of durable progression.
  4. Bind WBP_Stats and HUD XP display to progression delegates, and enemy/quest reward owners to the backend receipt pathway.
  5. Reopen equipment/talent/GAS consumers to call RebuildDerivedStats after committed build revisions; do not stack a second permanent effect on every refresh.

Required sequence: create native prerequisites -> actual build -> child/data creation -> configure -> assign to listed consumer -> save -> run named fixture. A compiled shell without its consumer assignment is not feature completion.

Functions, commands and event bindings

Project custom contracts are not engine/plugin nodes. A read-only asset participates through its consumer; it does not inherit that consumer’s mutation methods. Backend endpoint pages label transport proposals explicitly.

ContractExecution / effect
ApplyXPReceipt(RewardReceipt) -> Updated|AlreadyApplied; committed backend resultNative current owner; local request versus server validation as the command states. Backend work is asynchronous, cosmetics observe only after accepted state.
ResolveLevel(CumulativeXP, CurveVersion) -> Level; deterministic pure ruleNative current owner; local request versus server validation as the command states. Backend work is asynchronous, cosmetics observe only after accepted state.
RebuildDerivedStats(BuildSnapshot) -> ValidatedAttributes|InvalidBuild; serverNative current owner; local request versus server validation as the command states. Backend work is asynchronous, cosmetics observe only after accepted state.
ApplyProfessionXP(ProfessionId, VerifiedCommand) -> Updated|Rejected; part of gather/craft/fish transactionNative current owner; local request versus server validation as the command states. Backend work is asynchronous, cosmetics observe only after accepted state.

Lifecycle and cleanup

  1. Construct with only safe defaults; no service calls or world scans from construction scripts.
  2. Inject current owner/definition/session and subscribe once after readiness. Possession and replicated state may arrive in either order; guard initialization.
  3. Accept only permitted commands under current identity/epoch; keep local UI/cosmetic prediction separate from committed state.
  4. After server/backend result apply only matching request generation and nonstale revision; late reply to old body does not mutate new body.
  5. On death, transfer, disconnect, restart or teardown cancel transient work, clear input/timers, unbind delegates and release weak observers. Durable receipts remain authoritative.
  6. On reconnect create fresh runtime objects from current committed snapshot; never deserialize old Actor/widget pointers or rerun initial grants.

Concrete player-to-authority flow

Participation in Levels, derived stats and profession progression. Rule owner: URPGProgressionComponent. This asset’s role is Character XP/levels and profession skill are separate durable tracks. The level cap is data-defined; derived combat attributes are rebuilt from class growth, level, equipment, talents and valid effects rather than saved as competing authoritative totals.

  1. A verified defeat/quest/gather/craft/fish command produces a durable XP delta under its domain rule, never from a UI animation.
  2. Backend applies delta once and validates the threshold-table version; level changes and earned skill-point changes are returned in the same result.
  3. Zone updates progression cache and rebuilds derived attribute inputs through the one GAS initialization/modifier path.
  4. Health/max-resource changes follow an explicit policy: preserve current percentage on a max-stat rebuild while clamping bounds; do not fully heal on equipment swap.
  5. Owner UI displays XP/level and a level-up cue keyed to receipt/revision; remote nameplates see only public level.
  6. At cap, stop character XP progression under the chosen cap policy while allowing professions/quests/items to remain useful; no impossible prerequisite beyond cap.

Named fixture and acceptance

Fixture: L_Rillmere / Character_A / XPGrantFixture. Configure this asset at its first phase and run the linked phase recipe. Actual result: not run in Unreal/backend during documentation generation.

Stimulus / expected result
Replay XP receipt -> unchanged cumulative XP.
Threshold table contains duplicate/decreasing row -> content validator fails before admission.
Equip/unequip repeatedly -> identical final stats, no accumulated hidden bonuses.
At level 50 receive XP -> declared cap result, no level 51 or negative bar.

Record expected/observed separately. Reopen the concrete map consumer; inspect authoritative state, stable IDs/revisions and UI. Static link checks cannot satisfy this gameplay test.

Common mistakes and staged limits

Do not duplicate a native rule in Blueprint, assume a planned type is compiled, or keep callbacks/owners valid after world or session replacement.

Do not build later references as empty shells in an earlier phase. Source-derived art rows remain blocked by the missing ZIP; plugin API bindings remain blocked by installed-source verification. Placeholder visuals and proposed tuning are explicitly not production proof.
